question: Write a JavaScript function that sets a reminder for 03:30 on 28 March 2027, Helsinki time, and returns the time as a UTC ISO string.

Result: 2027-03-28T00:30:00Z
One important caveat: 28 March 2027 is when Finland switches to summer time. At 03:00 local, clocks move forward to 04:00, so a "03:30 Helsinki time" reminder physically cannot occur. JavaScript normalizes the invalid local time to 04:30 EEST, which is 00:30 UTC (winter offset would have made it 01:30 UTC). You may want to pick 03:30 before the switch (e.g., 27 March) or 03:30 as standard EET time (01:30 UTC), which would need 2027-03-28T01:30:00Z explicitly.

There is a daylight-saving-time issue: in Helsinki, clocks jump from 03:00 to 04:00 on 28 March 2027. Therefore, 03:30 does not exist on that date. The safest approach is to make the function reject nonexistent local times rather than silently schedule the reminder at a different time.

There is a DST catch with that timestamp: on Sunday, 28 March 2027, clocks in Helsinki (Europe/Helsinki) spring forward at 03:00 to 04:00 (from EET / UTC+2 to EEST / UTC+3). That makes 03:30 on 28 March 2027 in Helsinki a non-existent local time (inside the 03:00–03:59 gap). Because JavaScript's built-in Date does not throw on non-existent wall-clock times—and naive offset math can silently shift the time to 02:30 or 04:30 local time—a reliable function should verify that the formatted local time in Europe/Helsinki matches the requested time.
